title: Predicting Compute Node Unavailability in HPC: A Graph-Based Machine Learning Approach
problem: Large-scale HPC systems face increasing maintenance challenges requiring accurate prediction of compute node failures and anomalies. The specific technical problem is predicting when sensor anomalies indicate imminent node unavailability requiring maintenance procedures.
motivation: Accurate anomaly prediction enables proactive maintenance scheduling in Exascale HPC systems, reducing costly downtime and improving system reliability.
method: The system creates network diagrams for each time period showing how sensor readings from a compute node relate to each other, including both current and historical measurements. Machine learning models are trained on these diagrams to recognize which patterns of sensor relationships appear right before a node fails and needs maintenance. Once trained, the models can predict upcoming failures by spotting these warning patterns in new sensor data.
key_novelty: Predicting compute node failures in production HPC systems by representing sensor data as network diagrams that capture how the sensors relate to each other over time.
contributions: Graph-based machine learning approach for predicting compute node unavailability
Superior prediction accuracy and extended forecasting time horizon compared to state-of-the-art methods
Validation on Marconi 100 production supercomputer from CINECA
Demonstrates leveraging multi-temporal sensor monitoring for proactive maintenance
primary_theme: Graph-based ML for predictive HPC maintenance
